output.title: Typical wait time for a member callback
output.draft_text:
Q: How long does a member usually wait for a callback?

A: When a member requests a callback, they can usually expect to hear back within [standard callback time frame, e.g., number of business hours or business days]. Callbacks are made during [callback hours of operation and time zone].

Wait times may be longer [conditions that extend wait times, e.g., peak enrollment periods, high call volume, or requests needing research by another department]. In those cases, the member can expect a callback within [extended callback time frame].

If the request is urgent [definition of an urgent request, e.g., a member at the pharmacy counter or an imminent procedure], [urgent request handling, e.g., warm transfer, priority queue, or escalation path] applies, and the member should be contacted within [urgent callback time frame].

If the member has not received a callback within the expected time frame, the advocate should [follow-up or escalation steps]. When setting expectations, tell the member [approved wording for setting callback expectations] and confirm the best phone number and time to reach them.

If a callback attempt is missed, [number of callback attempts] attempts are made, and [what happens after unsuccessful attempts, e.g., voicemail, secure message, or case closure].

[callback hours of operation and time zone]
[conditions that extend wait times, e.g., peak enrollment periods, high call volume, or requests needing research by another department]

author_checklist: Confirm the official standard callback time frame and whether it is measured in business hours, business days, or calendar days.
Confirm whether the time frame is a contractual or regulatory commitment (for example, a service-level agreement or state or CMS requirement), or an internal target only.
Confirm whether callback times differ by plan type, line of business, client, or request type (for example, pharmacy, claims, or benefits questions).
Confirm callback hours of operation and the time zone used.
Confirm the definition of urgent requests and the approved priority or escalation process.
Confirm the escalation steps for members who have not received a callback within the expected window.
Confirm the number of callback attempts and what happens when attempts are unsuccessful.
Confirm the approved language advocates should use when setting expectations, and avoid promising exact times if they are not guaranteed.
Confirm the correct knowledge base and owner. Move this unit from benefits to pharmacy if callbacks are pharmacy-specific.
Verify that no existing policy or procedure conflicts with this content before approval.
